CPLX0-7794.label: 3-sulfolactaldehyde reductase
CPLX0-7794.comment:
3-Sulfolactaldehyde reductase (YihU) catalyzes the NADH-dependent reduction of (2R)-3-sulfolactaldehyde to 3-sulfopropanediol, which is excreted from the cell [Denger14].

Screening for enzymatic activity by metabolite profiling suggested that YihU has γ-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase activity. In vitro, the enzyme preferentially catalyzes the reaction in the succinate semialdehyde (SSA) reductase direction. YihU may play a role in detoxification of SSA [Saito09].

Expression of YihU is induced by growth on 6-sulfo-D-quinovose [Denger14]. A yihU deletion mutant is more sensitive to toxic levels of SSA than wild type [Saito09].

EG11845-MONOMER.label: sulfoquinovose isomerase
EG11845-MONOMER.comment:
Sulfoquinovose isomerase (YihS) catalyzes the first step in the degradation of 6-sulfo-D-quinovose, the isomerization to 6-deoxy-6-sulfo-D-fructose [Denger14].

YihS has mannose isomerase activity in vitro. Predicted active site residues were analyzed by site-directed mutagenesis. A crystal structure of the enzyme has been solved at 2.5 Å resolution [Itoh08].

YihS may be identical to the enzyme first identified by [Stevens76, Stevens81], although the quarternary structure differs. The mannose isomerase identified in [Stevens81] is a tetramer in solution, while YihS is a hexamer [Itoh08].

Expression of YihS is induced by growth on sulfoquinovose [Denger14]. A yihS mutant is unable to grow on sulfoquinovose as the sole source of carbon [Denger14].

EG11846-MONOMER.label: 6-deoxy-6-sulfofructose-1-phosphate aldolase
EG11846-MONOMER.comment:
6-Deoxy-6-sulfofructose-1-phosphate aldolase (YihT) catalyzes the third step in the degradation of 6-sulfo-D-quinovose, the cleavage of 6-deoxy-6-sulfo-D-fructose 1-phosphate to yield glycerone phosphate and (2R)-3-sulfolactaldehyde [Denger14].

Expression of YihT is induced by growth on sulfoquinovose [Denger14]. A yihT mutant is unable to grow on sulfoquinovose as the sole source of carbon [Denger14].

EG11848-MONOMER.label: 6-deoxy-6-sulfofructose kinase
EG11848-MONOMER.comment:
6-Deoxy-6-sulfofructose kinase (YihV) catalyzes the second step in the degradation of 6-sulfo-D-quinovose, the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of 6-deoxy-6-sulfo-D-fructose to 6-deoxy-6-sulfo-D-fructose 1-phosphate [Denger14].

Expression of YihV is induced by growth on sulfoquinovose [Denger14]. A yihV mutant is unable to grow on sulfoquinovose as the sole source of carbon [Denger14].

PWY-7446.label: sulfoquinovose degradation I
PWY-7446.comment:
Sulfoquinovose is a major component of organo-sulfur compounds in nature [Harwood79]. It is synthesized by higher plants, mosses, ferns, algae and most photosynthetic bacteria and serves as the polar headgroup of the sulfolipid in photosynthetic membranes [Benning98, Benning07].

Bacteria that are able to utilize sulfoquinovose as their sole source of carbon and energy for growth have been isolated. As of 2015, two degradation pathways have been described. One pathway is analogous to glycolysis (this pathway) while the other is analogous to the Entner-Doudoroff pathway (see sulfoquinovose degradation II).

About this pathway

It was recently shown that E. coli can also utilize 6-sulfo-D-quinovose as its sole source of carbon and energy for growth. The enzymes involved in this pathway were initially identified by analysis of differences in the proteomes of cultures grown with glucose vs. sulfoquinovose [Denger14].

sulfoquinovose isomerase catalyzes the initial isomerization of 6-sulfo-D-quinovose to 6-deoxy-6-sulfo-D-fructose. 6-deoxy-6-sulfofructose kinase phosphorylates 6-deoxy-6-sulfo-D-fructose to 6-deoxy-6-sulfo-D-fructose 1-phosphate, which is cleaved by 6-deoxy-6-sulfofructose-1-phosphate aldolase to form glycerone phosphate and 3-sulfolactaldehyde. 3-sulfolactaldehyde reductase reduces 3-sulfolactaldehyde to 3-sulfopropanediol (DHPS) in an NADH-dependent reaction.

The final products of this pathway are glycerone phosphate, which powers the cell via glycolysis I (from glucose 6-phosphate), and DHPS, which is excreted and can be further degraded by other bacteria.
